title: Copiag
summary: Copiag names a Babylon neck of land south of the old settlement of Breslau. The name survives in modern Copiague and Copiague Neck.
address_label: Copiague Neck, Babylon, NY (approximate general location)
map_geometry_source: Copiag is identified as a neck of land in western Babylon, south of old Breslau. Point uses a modern approximate Copiague Neck landform coordinate and is not a surveyed historic boundary.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Copiag, Coppiage, Copyag, Cuppuauge, and Copiague. The name is interpreted as land shut in, a place of shelter, or a harbor, connecting it with related forms such as Copeces and Copwax.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are crucial elements of shared understandings of Country, history, culture, rights and responsibilities.”

— Grace Karskens, A deep human history: remapping Darug place names and culture on Dyarubbin (2021), Naming Country section
land_loss_content: Copiag shows how Native names for sheltered necks, meadows, and waterways remained in colonial land records and later softened into modern community names. The name connects present-day Copiague to older Indigenous geography on the Great South Bay shore.
whereintheworld_content: Sources associate Copiag with the neck of land now called Copiague Neck. The exact boundaries of the seventeenth-century meadow and upland transactions remain uncertain.
